From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions (Harbourglass Ventures)

**Scope:** This reviews the Seller's SPA update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the Buyer baseline: 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24.0m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. I haven't seen the full SPA draft, so clause references follow the Seller's update. Suggested figures and periods are negotiating positions for the deal team to calibrate. Statutory points should be confirmed by NSW and privacy counsel before we rely on them.

---

## 1. Overall assessment

The package is built to put almost all known risk on the Buyer. The problems compound:

- **Known issues are excluded twice.** Clause 8.3 (anti-sandbagging) bars claims for anything the Buyer knew of, and the general data-room disclosure (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1) discloses everything in the data room. Since the Buyer now knows about Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the privacy incident and the supplier renewals, warranty protection for those items is effectively gone.
- **The cap and thresholds are too low for the known exposure.** The general cap is AUD 4.8m (20%). Bluefen revenue is about AUD 3.6m a year (~30%), and Riverlark is about AUD 3.2m. The Seller's package would leave the Buyer carrying most of these risks.
- **Several items are described as "ordinary course" or "adequate" without support.** The Seller's characterisations, particularly on the privacy incident and Ironquay, are not supported by the disclosure letter's own wording.

The right response is not to mark up individual clauses alone. The Buyer should reject the general regime as drafted and require specific indemnities, price/CP mechanics and escrow for the known items.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

**Cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m for general warranties.**
- Inadequate given the known exposures. Market practice for a private company deal is often a cap at or near the purchase price for general warranties; a Buyer opening position would be 100%.
- *Pushback:* 100% of price for general warranties. Fallback should not go below around 50% and must be tied to specific indemnities that sit outside the cap.

**Thresholds (cl 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket (excess only).**
- A deductible basket means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of all warranty losses, roughly 1% of price. Combined with a de minimis, small related claims may fall out entirely.
- *Pushback:* Tipping basket (first dollar recovery once the threshold is exceeded), de minimis of around AUD 10k, and aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts so they can't be split below the de minimis. Confirm that de minimis claims count toward the basket.

**Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13): general warranties notified within 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims".**
- 18 months is short for a warranty package covering tax, privacy, IP and contracts. Some issues (tax audits, privacy regulator action, IP ownership disputes) may surface after 18 months.
- The "applies to all Claims" wording would drag fundamental warranties and tax claims into the general 18-month regime.
- *Pushback:* General warranties: at least 36 months. Fundamental/title/capacity: 6 years, or the statutory period plus margin. Tax: 60 days after the relevant limitation period expires. The general regime should only apply to general warranties, expressly.

**Fundamental/title subject to general caps (Seller "administrative simplicity").**
- Reject. Title and capacity warranties go to the core of what the Buyer is buying. Capping them at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month life is not acceptable.
- *Pushback:* Uncapped or capped at 100% of price, with a 6-year period.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).**
- Unacceptable as drafted. Fraud cannot be excluded by contract, and a non-reliance clause should not operate to shield fraudulent or misleading pre-contract conduct. Specific indemnities and equitable remedies (including specific performance of completion obligations) should not be limited by the general regime.
- *Pushback:* Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, tax indemnity, title/capacity and any non-excludable statutory rights. Get NSW counsel to confirm the interaction with Australian Consumer Law and the Corporations Act before finalising the non-reliance wording.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1 and 1.2).**
- Disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, plus the Accounts and public registers, is a blanket disclosure that guts the warranties. The Buyer cannot warrant against what it cannot identify.
- *Pushback:* Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Require disclosure to be specific, fair, and made against a specific warranty. Accounts disclosure should be limited to specific line items, and the Buyer should retain the right to rely on the Accounts warranties.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).**
- Anti-sandbagging is the single most damaging clause here, because the Buyer's diligence has identified these issues. Under Australian common law the position on sandbagging is not settled, so the SPA should say expressly what the parties intend.
- *Pushback:* Delete cl 8.3. Insert an express pro-sandbagging clause: Buyer knowledge does not prejudice any claim. Where the Buyer knows of a specific issue and wants protection, it should use a specific indemnity or price mechanism, not a warranty claim.

### C. Known specific issues

**Bluefen (DL 2; cl 3 / 6.3): consent not obtained; conditions 11.3 unsatisfied; Seller to use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.**
- This is a value risk, not just a warranty point. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue. Consent conditions under cl 11.2/11.3 are unresolved, and nothing in the disclosure says Bluefen has agreed to continue.
- The "deemed satisfied" wording is a problem. It is unclear whether the consent must be in a form acceptable to the Buyer, whether all 11.3 conditions must be met, and whether the Buyer can waive.
- *Pushback:*
  - Bluefen consent (in agreed form, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by the Buyer) as a condition precedent, not a deemed satisfaction.
  - "All reasonable endeavours" with the Seller bearing reasonable costs, and no inducement payments without Buyer consent.
  - If consent isn't obtained, a Buyer walk right or a price adjustment/escrow.
  - Specific indemnity for loss of Bluefen revenue or termination within a defined post-completion period.

**Riverlark (DL 3; cl 2 / 7): ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; facility not repaid; release "to be provided following Completion".**
- In a debt-free/cash-free deal, the Seller should pay the debt out of the price at Completion. A post-completion release leaves security over the company's assets with the Buyer owning the company and the Seller holding the cash.
- *Pushback:* Payout letter and discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion, with the payout amount deducted from the price in the funds flow. Riverlark change-of-control consent under cl 8.1 must also be addressed. If any residual debt or fees survive, they must be Seller liabilities through specific indemnity.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller calls it "adequate".**
- DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. The Buyer may therefore not own some of the code or materials it is buying, and the indemnity covers only the fee, not the ownership risk.
- *Pushback:*
  - Make a confirmatory assignment of all Project Materials (and evidence of payment of all SOW fees, or payment from the price) a condition precedent.
  - Specific indemnity covering IP ownership, infringement and third-party claims arising from Ironquay work, not just the SOW3 fee, with a separate uncapped (or price-capped) limit and an extended survival period.
  - Consider retention/escrow until assignment is confirmed.

**Employee bonuses (DL 5): AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses, not in the draft funds flow; no statement on payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs.**
- These are transaction-related payments. If they fall due on Completion and are not in the funds flow, the Buyer may end up paying them through the company.
- *Pushback:* Treat them, together with payroll tax, superannuation, and on-costs, as Seller-borne debt-like items deducted from the price in the funds flow. Add a specific indemnity for any unfunded or later-arising employee entitlements linked to the transaction. Confirm NSW payroll tax position with the tax team.

**Privacy/export incident (DL 6; DD-006): download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); investigation preliminary; Seller says "not expected to be material".**
- The Seller's characterisation is not supported by its own disclosure. Names and contact details of ~1,240 individuals, sent to an external address, is a potential eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme. The 30-day assessment window may already have run given the 22 September date. This needs urgent verification.
- Exposure includes OAIC investigation and penalties, notification and remediation costs, and potential class action or individual claims.
- *Pushback:*
  - Require a completed forensic investigation and a documented NDB assessment before signing, with access logs for the file.
  - Specific indemnity, uncapped (or capped at price), covering regulatory fines, notification costs, remediation, third-party claims and related costs, with a long survival period.
  - Privacy compliance warranties (not subject to the general regime).
  - Escrow or retention sized to the investigation outcome.

**Office lease (DL 7): notification obligation identified; no statement on whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale.**
- *Pushback:* Confirm in writing whether the lease has a change-of-control trigger. If so, landlord consent or waiver as a condition precedent. Specific indemnity for any lease termination, make-good or consent costs.

**Supplier renewals (DL 8; DD-008 / DD-011): three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate); described as "ordinary-course operating costs".**
- The three renewals are apparently related, and each sits just above the 25k de minimis and below any threshold individually. The disclosure does not say whether they are terminable, accrued or non-cancellable beyond Completion.
- *Pushback:* Require disclosure of term, termination rights and whether any renewal runs past Completion. Costs attributable to pre-Completion periods should be Seller items. Any non-cancellable post-Completion commitments should be treated as a price or working-capital adjustment. Aggregate related contracts for disclosure and warranty purposes.

**Mossvale (DL 9): restriction on assignment; no statement that consent is required merely because shares are sold.**
- *Pushback:* Confirm that the agreement has no change-of-control trigger. If it does, consent as a CP or a specific indemnity.

**Title (DL 10; DD-012): share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100%; Seller relies on the register.**
- A share register is not conclusive title evidence on its own. The Buyer needs to verify encumbrances and the chain of title.
- *Pushback:*
  - Original share certificates (if issued) and executed transfer forms.
  - Current ASIC company extract and a PPSA/PPSR search over the shares for security interests.
  - Title warranty uncapped (see above) and a confirmation that no options, pre-emptive rights or other interests exist over the shares.
  - Confirm the stamp duty allocation for the share transfer.

**Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime").**
- The Seller treats tax and IP as covered by the general regime, which is inadequate given the Ironquay and privacy issues.
- *Pushback:* A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (uncapped or price-capped, outside the basket and de minimis, with statute-based survival). Full tax warranties, not limited to general claims. Separate IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and open-source use.

---

## 3. Recommendations summary

**Reject outright:**
1. Anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3); replace with an express pro-sandbagging clause.
2. General disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2).
3. Applying the general cap, basket and 18-month period to fundamental, title, capacity and tax claims.
4. Blanket application of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to all claims, including fraud.
5. Treating Bluefen consent as "satisfied" on delivery of a counterparty letter.
6. The post-Completion Riverlark release; require payout and discharge at Completion.
7. "Adequate" and "not expected to be material" characterisations of Ironquay and the privacy incident.

**Counter-propose:**
1. General warranty cap: 100% of price (fallback no lower than around 50%).
2. Tipping basket, de minimis around AUD 10k, aggregation of related claims.
3. General warranty period: at least 36 months. Fundamental/title/capacity: 6 years. Tax: 60 days after the limitation period.
4. Fundamental/title and tax: uncapped or capped at price, outside the general regime.
5. Fraud and specific indemnities carved out of all limitations.

**Specific indemnities (outside the general cap, basket and de minimis; with escrow or retention where indicated):**
- Bluefen revenue loss or termination post-completion (plus consent as CP).
- Riverlark and any residual debt (payout at Completion).
- Ironquay IP ownership and SOW fees (confirmatory assignment as CP).
- Employee bonuses, payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs (price deduction plus indemnity).
- Privacy/export incident: regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs.
- Lease, Mossvale and supplier renewal exposures, as determined by the Buyer's further enquiries.
- Pre-Completion tax.

**Conditions precedent and pre-signing actions:**
1. Forensic report and NDB assessment for the privacy incident; check urgently whether notification deadlines have passed.
2. Bluefen written consent in agreed form with all 11.3 conditions met.
3. Riverlark payout letter and PPSR discharge.
4. Ironquay confirmatory IP assignment and evidence of SOW payments.
5. Landlord and Mossvale position letters.
6. Title verification (certificates, ASIC extract, PPSR search).
7. Revised funds flow showing the Riverlark payout, bonuses and related on-costs as Seller-borne items.

**Price and structure:** Consider a price adjustment or escrow sized to the combined unquantified and contingent exposures (Bluefen revenue risk, privacy, Ironquay IP, bonuses, supplier commitments). The Buyer should size this with its financial and tax advisers; I have not quantified it here.

**Next steps:** Send the Seller a mark-up that rejects the general regime and proposes the specific indemnity and CP package above. Engage NSW corporate counsel on the non-reliance and sandbagging drafting, and privacy counsel on the NDB position as a priority.

**Mossvale (DL 9): restriction on assignment; no statement that consent is required merely because shares are sold.**
- *Pushback:* Confirm that the agreement has no change-of-control trigger. If it does, consent as a CP or a specific indemnity.

**Title (DL 10; DD-012): share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100%; Seller relies on the register.**
- A share register is not conclusive title evidence on its own. The Buyer needs to verify encumbrances and the chain of title.
- *Pushback:*
  - Original share certificates (if issued) and executed transfer forms.
  - Current ASIC company extract and a PPSA/PPSR search over the shares for security interests.
  - Title warranty uncapped (see above) and a confirmation that no options, pre-emptive rights or other interests exist over the shares.
  - Confirm the stamp duty allocation for the share transfer.

**Tax and IP (Seller: "settled under the general regime").**
- The Seller treats tax and IP as covered by the general regime, which is inadequate given the Ironquay and privacy issues.
- *Pushback:* A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (uncapped or price-capped, outside the basket and de minimis, with statute-based survival). Full tax warranties, not limited to general claims. Separate IP warranties covering ownership, non-infringement and open-source use.

## 3. Recommendations summary

**Reject outright:**
1. Anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3); replace with an express pro-sandbagging clause.
2. General disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2).
3. Applying the general cap, basket and 18-month period to fundamental, title, capacity and tax claims.
4. Blanket application of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to all claims, including fraud.
5. Treating Bluefen consent as "satisfied" on delivery of a counterparty letter.
6. The post-Completion Riverlark release; require payout and discharge at Completion.
7. "Adequate" and "not expected to be material" characterisations of Ironquay and the privacy incident.

**Counter-propose:**
1. General warranty cap: 100% of price (fallback no lower than around 50%).
2. Tipping basket, de minimis around AUD 10k, aggregation of related claims.
3. General warranty period: at least 36 months. Fundamental/title/capacity: 6 years. Tax: 60 days after the limitation period.
4. Fundamental/title and tax: uncapped or capped at price, outside the general regime.
5. Fraud and specific indemnities carved out of all limitations.

**Specific indemnities (outside the general cap, basket and de minimis; with escrow or retention where indicated):**
- Bluefen revenue loss or termination post-completion (plus consent as CP).
- Riverlark and any residual debt (payout at Completion).
- Ironquay IP ownership and SOW fees (confirmatory assignment as CP).
- Employee bonuses, payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs (price deduction plus indemnity).
- Privacy/export incident: regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party costs.
- Lease, Mossvale and supplier renewal exposures, as determined by the Buyer's further enquiries.
- Pre-Completion tax.

**Conditions precedent and pre-signing actions:**
1. Forensic report and NDB assessment for the privacy incident; check urgently whether notification deadlines have passed.
2. Bluefen written consent in agreed form with all 11.3 conditions met.
3. Riverlark payout letter and PPSR discharge.
4. Ironquay confirmatory IP assignment and evidence of SOW payments.
5. Landlord and Mossvale position letters.
6. Title verification (certificates, ASIC extract, PPSR search).
7. Revised funds flow showing the Riverlark payout, bonuses and related on-costs as Seller-borne items.

**Price and structure:** Consider a price adjustment or escrow sized to the combined unquantified and contingent exposures (Bluefen revenue risk, privacy, Ironquay IP, bonuses, supplier commitments). The Buyer should size this with its financial and tax advisers; I have not quantified it here.

**Next steps:** Send the Seller a mark-up that rejects the general regime and proposes the specific indemnity and CP package above. Engage NSW corporate counsel on the non-reliance and sandbagging drafting, and privacy counsel on the NDB position as a priority.
